title: Measurement of Maximum Isometric Force Generated by Permeabilized Skeletal Muscle Fibers
protocol: In a 1,000 ml beaker add 800 ml of deionized water.
Maintaining a gentle stir, add all the compounds listed in Table 1 to the deionized water and allow them to dissolve.
Bring to a final volume of 1,000 ml with deionized water.
Store the stock solution at 4 °C.
To make 200 ml of storage solution, begin with 100 ml of dissecting and storage stock solution in a 250 ml beaker.
Add sufficient Na2H2ATP to bring final adenosine triphosphate (ATP) concentration to 2 mM.
Bring to a final volume of 200 ml with glycerol.
Adjust to pH 7.00 with potassium hydroxide (KOH).
Store the storage solution at -20 °C.
Make dissecting solution by adding sufficient Na2H2ATP to bring final ATP concentration to 2 mM in the stock solution.
Adjust pH to 7.00 with KOH.
Bring the final volume to 200 ml with deionized water for the dissecting solution.
Aliquot the dissecting solution in volumes of 2.5 ml and store at -80°C.
Add 1 g of Brij 58 (0.5% w/v) to 200 ml of the dissecting solution in a beaker while stirring gently until dissolved for the dissecting solution with Brij 58.
Aliquot the dissecting solution with Brij 58 in volumes of 2.5 ml and store at -80°C.
Prepare three separate 1,000 ml beakers labeled "Relaxing", "Pre-activating" and "Activating".
Add 400 ml of deionized water to each beaker.
Heat the solutions to between 70 °C and 80 °C after adding compounds indicated in Table 2.
Cool the relaxing, pre-activating, and activating solutions to room temperature.
Add sufficient NaN3/KOH to bring the final NaN3 concentration to 1 mM in each solution.
Adjust pH to approximately 7.10 using KOH.
Add Na2H2ATP to bring the final ATP concentration to 8 mM in each solution.
Add Na2CrP to bring the final creatine phosphate (CrP) concentration to 10 mM in each solution.
Bring each solution to a final volume of 500 ml using deionized water.
Chill or heat the solutions to the temperature at which experiments will be performed.
Use KOH to bring the pH to 7.10 while maintaining that temperature.
Add relaxing solution to the pre-activating solution such that the final ratio is 1 part relaxing solution in 500 parts of pre-activating solution.
Aliquot the solution in volumes of 2.5 ml and store at -80°C.
Begin with a strand of non-sterile USP 10-0 monofilament nylon suture.
Use forceps to create a loop using the double overhand knot technique.
Reduce the knot size to approximately 750 µm diameter.
Assess the loop diameter under the microscope using eyepiece graticule markings.
Use microdissecting scissors to remove excess suture, leaving only the loop and small (500 μm) tails on either side.
Repeat steps until 4 usable loops have been made.
Store loops in a silicone elastomer-plated petri dish for future use.
Obtain the sample of interest and transfer it to the facility where dissection will take place.
Transfer the sample to a petri dish containing chilled dissecting solution.
Ensure that the sample remains submerged by adding more dissecting solution if necessary.
Inspect the sample under the microscope.
Manipulate the sample to align the longitudinal axes of the fibers toward the right shoulder of the investigator.
Anchor the sample to the dish by pinning at the corners.
Use remaining connective tissue as anchoring points for dissection.
Dissect muscle bundle along longitudinal margins between fibers.
Pin bundle in slight tension if necessary.
Gently dissect smaller bundles measuring approximately 0.5-1 mm in width and ≥3 mm in length.
Assess dimensions of dissected bundles using a microscope with graticule markings or ruler.
Discard damaged tissue from dissection process.
Repeat dissection until sufficient number of bundles are obtained or sample is exhausted.
Transfer muscle bundles into vial containing 2.5 ml of chilled dissecting solution with Brij 58 added (0.5%, w/v).
Incubate on ice for 30 min with occasional gentle agitation.
Transfer the bundles to a vial containing fresh dissecting solution without Brij 58.
Agitate gently and briefly to remove any remaining detergent.
Transfer the bundles to a vial containing chilled storage solution.
Incubate overnight at 4 °C.
Prepare a storage box capable of withstanding -80 °C.
Fill individual 0.5 ml screw cap conical tubes with 200-400 µl of fresh storage solution.
Transfer the bundles into individually labeled conical tubes.
Ensure that the bundle is not stuck to the side or floating on top of the solution in each tube.
Cap the conical tubes.
Store the samples at -80 °C until testing.
Thaw one vial each of the relaxing, pre-activating and activating solutions and maintain on ice.
Prepare the microscope for use.
Prepare the testing apparatus for use.
Prepare the associated computer for use.
Fill the first experimental chamber with relaxing solution.
Thread two prepared suture loops onto the stainless steel attachment surfaces extending from both the force-transducer and length-controller.
Thaw a fiber bundle of interest, and transfer to a silicone elastomer-plated petri dish with fresh, chilled relaxing solution.
Secure the bundle with pins at either end.
Use forceps to grasp a fiber at one end.
Extract the fiber along its longitudinal axis.
Modify a pipet tip using a razor blade or scalpel.
Introduce the fiber into the modified pipet tip with relaxing solution.
Transfer the single fiber from the silicone elastomer-plated petri dish to the experimental chamber containing relaxing solution.
Remove the fiber from the pipet tip gently with forceps.
Anchor one end of the fiber to the length-controller using a suture loop.
Tighten the first suture loop around 1 mm to 2 mm from the end of the attachment surface on the length-controller.
Manipulate the fiber toward the force-transducer and secure it using the same procedure.
Remove excess suture using microdissecting scissors.
Place the fiber under a small amount of tension by adjusting the distance between the length-controller and force-transducer arms.
Thread the second loop over the first and anchor the fiber within 0.2 mm of the end of the force-transducer attachment surface.
Remove excess suture using microdissecting scissors.
Add more relaxing solution to ensure the surface is flat if necessary.
Align the fiber parallel to the sidewalls of the experimental chamber by adjusting the position in the y-axis direction.
Adjust the position of the length-controller in the z-axis direction until the fiber is parallel to the floor of the chamber.
Discard fibers that are contorted, twisted, or damaged during mounting.
Insert calibrated target screen onto the anterior aspect of the microscope over the first experimental chamber.
Turn on the laser and adjust the stage position so the laser passes through the center of the fiber.
Position the fiber with respect to the laser beam to observe an interference pattern on the calibrated target screen.
Turn off the lights to visualize the interference pattern more clearly.
Replace the fiber if no interference pattern is observed, indicating abnormal or damaged myofibrillar components.
Set the sarcomere length using the length-controller x-axis micrometer drive.
Measure the distance between the two innermost sutures using the digital readout on the micrometer drive.
Align the vertical cross hair of the eyepiece with the innermost border of one suture and zero the digital readout.
Translate the stage along the x-axis until reaching the other innermost suture.
Record the length indicated by the digital display as fiber length, Lf.
Maintain the fiber at Lf.
Use the microscope-mounted camera to capture a high magnification image of the central portion of the fiber from both the top view.
Capture side view images using the prism embedded in the side of the chamber.
Move the microscope only in the y-direction when shifting between top and side views.
Obtain measurements for normalizing absolute force later in the study.
Confirm that the temperature of the relaxing, pre-activating, and activating solutions is stable at 15 °C.
Use the chamber control software to move the fiber to the chamber containing the pre-activating solution.
Incubate the fiber in the pre-activating solution for 3 min.
With 10 sec remaining in the pre-activating solution and the fiber length maintained at Lf, establish a zero force level in the experimental record.
Move the fiber to the chamber containing the activating solution and allow maximum isometric force to develop as evidenced by a plateau in force that is preceded by a rapid rise.
Use the length-controller to identify the force-transducer output that corresponds to zero force in the chamber containing the activating solution.
Return the fiber to the chamber containing the relaxing solution following attainment of a second force plateau.
To test multiple fibers during any one session, aspirate all solutions and add new, chilled solutions.
